sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle. 1985. The Pipil Language of El Salvador (Mouton Grammar Library 1). Berlin: Mouton. Appendix on Guatemalan Nahua, section '1. Alagüilac'.
sources.note: Nothing on Alaguilac stress (there are no Alaguilac data). Argues Brinton's identification is false: Bromowicz's list and the manuscript leaves are San Agustín 'Mejicano' (central-Mexican Nahua, post-Conquest); colonial sources distinguish Alagüilac from Nahua and Chortí; Campbell suggests Xinkan on the basis of Xinka toponyms (Campbell 1972, 1978), citing Campbell 1972 and Fowler 1981 for discussion.

sources.citation: Brinton, Daniel G. 1887. On the so-called Alaguilac language of Guatemala. Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 24(126): 366-377.
sources.note: Nothing. Presents Bromowicz's 1878 word list from Dolores Corral of San Agustín Acasaguastlán and four 1610-1637 manuscript leaves; no accent marks, no remark on stress; concludes (p. 376) the language 'was a quite pure form of the Nahuatl'. Campbell 1985 shows these data are post-Conquest central-Mexican Nahua, not Alaguilac.

sources.citation: Stoll, Otto. 1884. Zur Ethnographie der Republik Guatemala. Zürich: Orell Füssli. Section 24 'Die Alagüilac-Sprache', p. 172.
sources.note: Nothing. States that only the name of the language is known ('Wir kennen zur Zeit von dieser Sprache... bloss den Namen') and that it was already extinct, Spanish only, at San Cristóbal Acasaguastlán.
